title: Blitz shift playbook notes and follow-ups
content:
Quick log from the 03:00-11:00 shift (blitz). Purpose: raw notes to capture triage, follow-ups, runbook gaps and concrete TODOs for later handoff. Not polished.

SUMMARY:
- Pager at 03:17: high tail latency on inference-hosts in eu-west-1 (p50 increased from ~45ms -> 300ms).
- New deploy to dedicated pool triggered rolling restarts + some nodes rebalanced -> correlated with increased queue lengths.
- Mitigated by routing 20% traffic to fallback model-variant and triggering controlled scale-up of dedicated pool.
- No customer-visible errors beyond elevated latency for ~7 minutes.

TIMELINE / Triage notes (logged as I worked):
- 03:17 ALERT: alert-slo-eu-latency > 5m. Pager: mobile + slack.
- 03:18 Jumped on #ops-realtime. Observed: cluster-monitor spikes in request-queue, NVidia GPU util 95% on 4 nodes, sudden KV cache miss rate up x3.
- 03:21 Check deploy history: rollout id deploy-2026-05-18-02:58 to dedicated-pool-eu. Canary completed at 03:10 per CI, but subsequent autoscaler started rebalancing at 03:14.
- 03:23 Exec commands run: `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-eu -o wide` -> a few pods in CrashLoopBackOff (OOMKilled on one), others very high memory.
- 03:25 Rolled routing: applied policy to route ~20% of production traffic to model-variant:small-quant which has lower memory/KV pressure.
- 03:27 Triggered scale-up: toggle reserve-capacity + requested one-off burst (+4 gpus) via infra runbook command.
- 03:30 Observed queue length decline, p50 latency back to ~80ms, p95 gradually decreased over next 4 minutes. Alert recovered 03:36.
- 03:40 Post-incident checks: logs indicate a specific inference-serving task spiked memory due to a batch size regression (new batching config in PR #789).

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS / NOTES TO SELF: (things to do before EOD / handoff)
- TODO: Add safe-guard in rollout pipeline to prevent autoscaler rebalancing before 10m quiet window after canary. Owner: Samir. Jira: JIRA-RELI-4567.
- TODO: Revert or patch PR #789 batching-change for dedicated pools until we validate memory profile. Owner: Maya. Quick revert PR template in repo: github.com/redwood/inference#pr-789.
- TODO: Update runbook section "dedicated-pool-burst" to include the exact `gcloud` command used in this incident for burst requests (missing snippet). Owner: Arjun.
- TODO: Add a one-line checklist for oncall to prefer route->variant small-quant earlier if queue > 75 percentile for 3 consecutive minutes. Owner: Oncall rotation.

RUNBOOK GAPS (raw):
- Lack of clear instruction on how to detect "batching config regression" from live metrics; only postmortem logic exists. Need a short diagnostic query (kusto/prom) that flags sudden per-host mem-per-batch increase.
- Dedicated-pool autoscaler doc lacks guidance on interacting with rollout system; currently two teams operate independently (release + infra). Add a joint workflow.
- Missing KMS note: when we triggered burst the key fetch logs spiked and added ~150ms to cold starts — unclear if expected.

COMMANDS & QUICK CHECKS I used (paste for runbook):
- kubectl -n dedicated-eu get pods -o wide | egrep "OOM|Crash|Running"
- kubectl -n dedicated-eu logs <pod> --since=15m | grep -i batch
- prometheus: sum(rate(request_queue_length[1m])) by (pool)
- kusto: inference_logs | where time > ago(15m) | summarize avg(mem_used_per_batch) by host
- infra: infra-cli burst reserve --region eu-west-1 --gpus 4 --reason "oncall emergency 2026-05-18"

FOLLOW-UPS / OWNER ASSIGNMENTS (concrete):
- Samir: Safeguard rollout gating (JIRA-RELI-4567). Target: patch + deploy by 2026-05-21.
- Maya: Revert PR #789 or submit fast patch that restores old batching defaults for dedicated pools. Target: 2026-05-19 midday.
- Arjun (me): Runbook edits: add commands above, small troubleshooting checklist, and a short blurb on when to route to model-variant(s). Target: EOD 2026-05-18.
- Izzy: Check KMS latency on burst flows and file a KMS-support ticket if >100ms cold-start latency consistently. Target: 2026-05-20.

NOTES FOR HANDOFF: (for next oncall)
- Incident resolved but root cause likely config regression in PR #789. Until patched, consider lowering parallel-batch cap in dedicated pools.
- Watchlist: dedicated-eu queue-length, model_variant_small-quant saturations, node memory usage. Set custom alert for mem-per-batch > 2x baseline.
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C08ABC1JK/p1684452000000 (summary pinned at top).

POST SHIFT RETROSPECTIVE POINTS (quick):
- Our automated canary check passed but didn't detect memory regression — extend canary to include memory-per-batch profiling for 5m.
- Consider adding a pre-rollout smoke that simulates high-batch inference patterns for dedicated pools.
- Improve observability of KV cache hit patterns — observed correlated spike but no quick graph in console.

MISC CLIPPINGS / personal reminders: 
- If I get paged again for similar spike: 1) route fallback variant, 2) increase capacity, 3) check for recent PRs touching batching. Keep those as checklist on phone.
- Sleep: try to stay offline after 12:00 local if possible — followup actions scheduled for daytime.

ROUGH DRAFT for runbook change (snippet to paste into confluence):
- Title: "Dedicated pool emergency mitigation"
- Steps:
  1) Confirm elevated queue (prom query) and p95>200ms for >3m.
  2) Identify recent rollout: infra-deploy list --last 60m.
  3) If recent config change touches batching or memory flags, route 20-30% traffic to model-variant:small-quant (runbooks/route-variant cmd).
  4) Request burst capacity: infra-cli burst reserve --region <region> --gpus 4 --reason \"oncall emergency\".
  5) If pods OOM, mark suspect and open revert PR ASAP.
  6) After recovery: file incident note + attach logs + schedule postmortem.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS: (to discuss in retro)
- Why did canary pass while memory-per-batch regressed? Canary tests are CPU/token-based but not memory profiling for batched flows.
- Is there a way to make KV cache metrics more prominent in dashboards?

END NOTES: saving raw so I can iterate. Will tidy a separate short customer-facing summary if needed.

-- Arjun
